newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees patents bill regulations by mid-Jan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees patents bill regulations by mid-Jan.

text.p: The Brazilian government expects to publish the regulatory framework for an already-approved patents bill by January 15, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles said.

Dornelles said the Brazilian Association of Intellectual Property (ABPI), in conjunction with the ministry, had already prepared five regulatory acts and the ministry would be open to further private sector suggestions until December 20.
"I'm sure that by January 15 we will be able to publish the acts," Dornelles told reporters.

After long controversy and sustained pressure from Washington, the Brazilian Congress approved a patents bill earlier this year bringing its intellectual property rights laws into line with Brasilia's international obligations.
The regulatory framework, which does not have to be approved by Congress, is supposed to come into effect by May 1997.
